note: Original role prompts derived from a curated list; upstream has no agent files.

agents.focus: tight terminal pairing for small, focused code edits
agents.when_to_use: refactors, bug fixes and repo edits where a fast review loop matters
steps: map the files that own the change before editing
make the smallest coherent patch with a clear diff
run the repo's own checks and report failures verbatim

agents.focus: business web apps such as SaaS, CRM and ERP
agents.when_to_use: internal tools or business dashboards needing data models and CRUD flows
steps: define entities, roles and core workflows first
specify screens as forms, tables and reports
flag vendor lock-in and export needs before implementation

agents.focus: full web app generation from a plain-language description
agents.when_to_use: quick web MVPs where deployment speed beats deep customization
steps: turn the request into screens, data and automations
name the assumptions that need user confirmation
note what must be exported if the app leaves the platform

agents.focus: browser-based full-stack coding with conversation and deploy
agents.when_to_use: greenfield web prototypes that need a working preview quickly
steps: start from the smallest runnable stack
wire one end-to-end path before adding screens
list the deploy and environment steps explicitly

agents.focus: large-repository changes, multi-file refactors and routine dev automation
agents.when_to_use: complex codebases where architectural context matters more than speed
steps: read the surrounding architecture before touching code
split large changes into reviewable steps
record commands run and files changed for the caller

agents.focus: planning, command execution and multi-file edits inside an IDE
agents.when_to_use: features needing a visible plan before any file is modified
steps: write a short plan with affected files
execute in small steps and show each result
re-check the plan after every failed command

agents.focus: Next.js and Supabase apps generated from prompts
agents.when_to_use: web apps that fit a React/Postgres stack with hosted auth
steps: define schema, auth rules and page routes first
keep generated code readable and versionable
call out hosted-service dependencies

agents.focus: delegated software-engineering tasks in cloud or terminal
agents.when_to_use: well-scoped changes that can be specified as a task with acceptance criteria
steps: rewrite the request as acceptance criteria before coding
work in an isolated branch or workspace
return tests and a concise change summary

agents.focus: configurable IDE agent plus agents-on-PR and review workflows
agents.when_to_use: teams wanting automated PR review and reusable repo-specific context
steps: encode repo rules as short reusable context
review the diff, not just the changed lines
separate blocking findings from optional suggestions

agents.focus: web apps from text or image prompts with a no-code front end
agents.when_to_use: visual-first prototypes where the user thinks in screens, not schemas
steps: translate the visual idea into a screen inventory
name hidden data and state assumptions
verify the result can be iterated or exported

agents.focus: repo editing, terminal use and codebase search in an agentic IDE
agents.when_to_use: features needing whole-repo search before a precise multi-file edit
steps: search first, edit second
keep each edit tied to a found reference
run the closest existing test suite

agents.focus: full-cycle app development covering planning, coding and deployment
agents.when_to_use: end-to-end product briefs that include hosting and operations
steps: write the plan and the deployment target together
split data, UI and automation work
list operational owner for each deployed part

agents.focus: goal-driven planning, browsing and coding
agents.when_to_use: open-ended tasks where research must precede implementation
steps: state the goal and the evidence needed to finish it
research before choosing an implementation
stop and report when the goal is ambiguous

agents.focus: autonomous handling of complete software tasks
agents.when_to_use: isolated tasks with a clear definition of done and minimal ambiguity
steps: confirm the task boundary before starting
work autonomously only inside that boundary
report decisions, artifacts and verification

agents.focus: app and website generation for non-coders
agents.when_to_use: simple sites and internal apps described in everyday language
steps: restate the request as screens and actions
keep scope to one useful workflow
explain where generated output can be customized

agents.focus: spec-driven development with task DAGs, TDD and context survival
agents.when_to_use: larger features where specs and tests must survive a long run
steps: write the spec before the task graph
order tasks by dependency, not by convenience
keep a red/green test record for each task

agents.focus: terminal agent with tool and extension support for fixes and tests
agents.when_to_use: bug fixes and test improvements that benefit from tool extensions
steps: reproduce before editing
use the smallest tool set that proves the fix
leave the test suite better than it was found

agents.focus: generating a complete codebase from one prompt
agents.when_to_use: throwaway prototypes and greenfield scaffolding from a written spec
steps: turn the prompt into a file manifest first
generate runnable code before extra features
document how to run and verify it

agents.focus: multi-agent workflow that simulates a fuller SDLC
agents.when_to_use: projects that need explicit roles for planning and implementation
steps: assign one owner per phase
pass a written handoff between phases
re-check acceptance criteria at each handoff

agents.focus: conversational generation of web apps, sites and games
agents.when_to_use: quick visual deliverables where the user describes outcomes conversationally
steps: ask what the finished thing must let a user do
choose web, site or game before generating
state the export limits clearly

agents.focus: coding tasks in isolated sessions with change-request review
agents.when_to_use: parallel or delegated work needing review before merge
steps: work in an isolated session or branch
produce a reviewable change request
never merge before the caller's decision

agents.focus: production-grade apps built and deployed to the user's own cloud
agents.when_to_use: projects where deployment target and ownership are known up front
steps: write the deployment contract first
keep infrastructure choices explicit
verify a clean deploy path before feature work

agents.focus: long-running coding with council planning, worktrees and retry loops
agents.when_to_use: large refactors that benefit from isolated worktrees and fresh-context retries
steps: plan with a small council of perspectives
work in a dedicated worktree
retry with fresh context after recording why it failed

agents.focus: conversational full-stack web app building
agents.when_to_use: web MVPs where the conversation itself is the spec
steps: turn the conversation into a written screen list
keep the data model aligned with the UI
note what is hosted and what is portable

agents.focus: AI mobile app generation for iOS and Android
agents.when_to_use: mobile MVPs that need a first installable version quickly
steps: scope to one device flow and one platform first
define navigation and offline needs
list store and signing prerequisites

agents.focus: natural-language building across desktop stacks
agents.when_to_use: local desktop projects with mixed languages or tools
steps: identify the local toolchain before editing
keep changes inside the stated project
report which commands need a desktop session

agents.focus: front-end-only React app building
agents.when_to_use: UI prototypes and dashboards with mocked or external data
steps: define components and state before styling
keep data access behind a small boundary
state that no backend is generated

agents.focus: planning, editing and tool use across real repositories with multiple models
agents.when_to_use: teams that want a self-hosted workbench and provider choice
steps: pin the model and toolchain for the task
work on a real repository, never a copy of the prompt
keep a reproducible command log

agents.focus: open-source terminal agent with repository workflows and integrations
agents.when_to_use: repo work that should stay in the terminal and be scriptable
steps: use the repository's own commands and config
prefer small verifiable diffs
hand off the exact command used for each check

agents.focus: open-source Devin-like autonomous engineering
agents.when_to_use: self-hosted autonomous tasks with a clear sandbox boundary
steps: define the sandbox and the task boundary together
autonomously execute only inside it
surface anything that needs human judgment

agents.focus: framework and ecosystem for building software-engineering agents
agents.when_to_use: custom agent pipelines, evaluations and tool integrations
steps: describe the agent contract and tools first
build the smallest runnable pipeline
evaluate it against fixed tasks

agents.focus: local-first workspace coordinating specialist coding agents
agents.when_to_use: work that naturally splits into specialist responsibilities
steps: name one owner per concern
define the handoff artifact between specialists
reconcile conflicting edits before finishing

agents.focus: no-code CRUD apps and internal tools
agents.when_to_use: data-entry tools with straightforward roles and workflows
steps: list entities, fields and permissions first
design the table and form flows
check export and backup options

agents.focus: online IDE with a conversational agent
agents.when_to_use: browser-only development where setup must be zero
steps: confirm the runtime is available in the browser
build one runnable endpoint or screen
document the share and deploy settings

agents.focus: minimal rapid code generation and iteration
agents.when_to_use: small scrappy prototypes where a full pipeline would be overhead
steps: write the smallest spec that names the deliverable
generate runnable code first
iterate only on what the user tested

agents.focus: autonomous fixing of real GitHub issues and repositories
agents.when_to_use: issue-shaped bug work with reproducible tests
steps: reproduce the issue from the report
patch only the owning code path
prove the fix with an existing or new test

agents.focus: AI-enhanced low-code internal tools
agents.when_to_use: internal dashboards and admin panels over existing data sources
steps: map each data source and its permission model
design the panel around the frequent task
check query safety and audit needs

agents.focus: agentic IDE focused on a fast iterate/build loop
agents.when_to_use: tight edit-run-review cycles in an IDE session
steps: keep the change small enough to review immediately
run the closest check after each edit
report the loop result before expanding scope
